articleTitle: Evaluation of the Electronic Nose Used for Monitoring Environmental Pollution
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Air pollution is a one of the major concern of civilized world, which has a significant impact on human health and the environment. Recent studies highlight that the exposure to polluted air can increase the incidence of diseases and deteriorate the quality of life. Hence, it is necessary to develop tools for real-time air quality monitoring. Electronic-nose systems based on sensors are an interesting and promising technology in the field of monitoring environmental pollution. However, real-life usage in monitoring of outdoor air is connected with several challenges, such as temperature or humidity changes affecting sensor response. In this study, a performance of the three electronic nose systems based on semiconducting gas sensors only, amperometric gas sensors only and both type of sensors in outdoor air quality is evaluated. Toxic gas concentration prediction ability of these three e-noses is compared with the reference results from the stationary station of air monitoring system.

articleTitle: CuO and CuO/TiO2-y Thin-Film Gas Sensors of H2 and NO2
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Thin films of CuO and CuO/TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> were deposited by medium frequency magnetron sputtering on a variety of substrates for the purposes of gas sensing applications. Film characterization was performed by means of X-ray diffraction, XRD, scanning electron microscopy, SEM, and optical spectrophotometry. Gas sensing measurements were carried out in NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> atmosphere at constant temperature chosen within the range of 200-400°C. Improvement in sensor response has been observed for CuO/TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> thin film heterostructures.

articleTitle: Multianalyte Calibration Methods for Potentiometric Integrated Sensors System for Determination of Ions Concentration in a Body Fluids
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: In recent years, integration and miniaturization of ion-selective electrodes (ISEs) have brought many benefits resulting in the possibility of simultaneous determination of the ions concentration in a small sample volume. One of the key problems related to the preparation of integrated sensors systems (ISSs) is a calibration procedure due to the necessity to calibrate each particular sensor separately. The main aim of the research was to develop a novel calibration method for ISSs fabricated with the use of an all-solid-state technology.

articleTitle: A Concept of MEMS Mass Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: This paper presents the concept of a MEMS mass spectrometer, which integrates all necessary modules on single vacuum-sealed chip. Computer simulations and preliminary studies showed that the miniature mass spectrometer containing a high vacuum micropump, a sample injection system, an ion source, an analyzer and a detector is possible to obtain. The spectrometer performs analysis in vacuum of range of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> hPa and we believe is able to distinguish all components at mass range of 1 to 100 units with reasonable accuracy.

articleTitle: Gas Sensing Properties of Reduced Graphene Oxide Modified by Copper Oxide
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Graphene oxide was obtained using the modified Hummers method. Some part of samples was prepared as multilayer graphene oxide - copper oxide structures. After temperature annealing the structures decreased the resistivity enabling investigations of interaction with the ambient gas. The response to nitrogen dioxide was determined and observed changes with varying measurement temperature and gas concentration explained.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Commercial Electrochemical Gas Sensors for the Monitoring of CO in Ambient Air
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Air pollution is a growing concern of civilized world, which has a significant impact on human health and the environment. Recent studies highlight that the exposure to polluted air can increase the incidence of diseases and deteriorate the quality of life. Hence, it is necessary to develop tools for real-time air quality monitoring. For air pollution monitoring a wide range of stationary gas and particulate analysers can be used. However, such instruments are relatively large, heavy and expensive. Only governments, local authorities and major industries can afford to use such devices. Instruments based on low cost gas sensors can be interesting and promising alternative. However, real-life usage of gas sensors in monitoring outdoor air is connected with several challenges, such as temperature or humidity changes affecting sensor response. In this study, a laboratory evaluation of commercially available electrochemical gas sensors for the monitoring of CO in ambient air is presented. Six commercial electrochemical CO sensors were tested simultaneously under controlled gas concentrations and various environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Inkjet 3D Printed Venturi Microflowmeter
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: In this paper we present a 3D printed flow meter based on venture tube. Diameter of printed microchannel is 800 um for wider and 400 um for smaller channel. Application of different types of pressure sensors were investigated: differential, absolute and digital barometer. Results of measurements for differential pressure/flow and calculation of liquid flow are showed. Presented microfluidic device can be also easily adapted for modular systems. The developed flow meter is the first demonstrator of integration of commercially available MEMS sensors and 3D printed microfluidics structure in one structure.

articleTitle: Inertial Measurements of Curling Stone Movement
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Curling is a winter Olympic sport, in which athletes slide 20-kilogram granite stones on the surface of ice to the target called “house”. An inertial measurement unit was attached to a curling stone handle in order to measure acceleration and rotation during a delivery. In this paper, we present the measurement system that consisted of accelerometers and a gyroscope as well as the results. Obtained results show that the movement of a curling stone has a high-frequency noise-like nature, which is likely to be caused by the stick-slip mechanism between the granite stone and the pebbled ice surface.

articleTitle: Determination of Oxygen Saturation Based on Distorted Photoplethysmography Signals by Scaling Method
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: This article presents a new method of estimation of a blood oxygen saturation, designed for use in high distorted photoplethysmography (PPG) signals in case of movement artefacts. This method is named Scaling Method (SM) and it is based on a calculated scaling factor between two PPG signals with various absorption coefficient. The SM method was designed to be used in wearable devices.

articleTitle: Point Defect Structure and Gas Sensing Properties of V2O5 Thin Films Deposited by RF Reactive Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>-undoped and V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>-Ti-doped thin films were deposited onto insulating support (either fused silica or alumina) by rf sputtering from vanadium and mosaic V-Ti in a reactive Ar+O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> atmosphere. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Scanning Electronic Microscopy (SEM) were used to structural and phase characterization. Electrical properties were determined by means of impedance spectroscopy method (0.1 Hz-1.4 MHz) at temperature from ambient (RT) to 620 K and oxygen partial pressure from 600 Pa to 21 kPa. The studied samples were characterized by an equivalent circuit composed of ohmic resistors and non Debye constant phase element. Undoped V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> layers show n-type semiconductor behavior, on the other hand V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>-Ti-doped are p-type. V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>-based thin films exhibited good response towards to flammable gases such as hydrogen.

articleTitle: Mechanical Characterization of Inkjet 3D Printed Microcantilevers
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: The paper presents results of characterization of inkjet 3D printed microcantilevers. Determination of mechanical properties of microstructures is a key issue towards application of the structures in the 3D printed sensors or actuators. Micro cantilevers with different length and thicknesses were designed, printed and characterized. Obtained results were coMPared to the computer simulations. Knowledge on the mechanical properties of 3D printed microcantilevers will allow to predict and evaluate the behavior of future designed structures applied in microsensors, microactuators.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Fluorescein as a Label in Electrochemical and Optical Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Fluorescein is a fluorescent dye, that is commonly used as a fluorescent label in biochemistry, environment protection and ophthalmology. Its fluorescent features are well known, while the knowledge about its electrochemical behavior is still negligible. In our research, we decided to investigate electrochemical activity of fluorescein and determine its concentration with the use of differential pulse voltammetry and spectrofluorimetry in order to compare the utility of each method for fluorescein detection, towards simultaneous optical and electrochemical detection of bioanalytes. Due to the strong effect of pH of the environment on the analyte properties, we utilized buffer solutions of various pH during all experiments. Results of the voltammetric measurements indicated that fluorescein is electrochemically active compound, with the electrochemical activity affected by the pH of environment. Fluorescein undergoes irreversible one-step electrochemical oxidation in the potential range from 0 V to 1.4 V on graphene screen-printed electrodes. Differential pulse voltammetric method allowed to successfully detect fluorescein at micromolar concentration levels. Comparison of the data obtained by each measurement method allowed claiming, that electrochemical methods are more suitable for fluorescein determination in the solutions of low pH, whereas spectrofluorimetric method is more advantageous in the case of alkaline solutions. The further research should be performed in the context of the study on electrochemical activity of fluorescein conjugated with bioanalytes e.g. antibody.

articleTitle: Wavelet Transform Analysis of Temperature Modulated Gas Sensor Response
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: The aim of the study was to evaluate whether it is possible to extract the information about the gas concentration despite the influence of humidity. Commercial semiconductor sensor response was examined under the application of a periodic temperature change. The data was collected using measurement protocol for different concentrations of ammonia at specified levels of relative humidity. In this work we focused on the evaluation of the Discrete Wavelet Transform analysis results obtained during experimental investigation of the single semiconductor gas sensor in the presence of humidified atmosphere containing ammonia. The results of the analysis show that proposed method enable the possibility of determine the low concentrations of ammonia.

articleTitle: Skydiver Flight Parameters Recorder
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: This paper presents skydiver flight parameters recorder named SKYBOX and data which can be acquired by it. It is unique device which can measure not only height profile and GPS track but body orientation also. The device can collect not only height and geographic position but also inertial information - accelerations and rotational speeds. Basic information about metrological specification of the device are presented. Additionally, sample data like height profile, GPS track and movement parameters are shown. It is shown that individual phases of the skydiver flight can be discriminated.

articleTitle: From a Microtip to a Planar Cathode — An Electron Source with a Simplified Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: For more than a decade we have been observing the significant growth in an electron source development for the vacuum nanoelectronics. Here, we discuss the progress in the electron source advancement with a simplified technology, performed in our laboratory and dedicated to a miniaturized MEMS-type transmission electron microscope.

articleTitle: OLED Display as a Useful Tool Towards Real-Time On-Chip Photosensitivity Investigation of Microorganisms
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: In the paper, the utility of OLED display towards real-time on-chip photosensitivity investigation of algae has been presented. The microorganisms have been cultured in the glass lab-on-a-chip and stimulated with red (615 nm) and blue (470 nm) light in the microchamber area. A notable photophobic response of euglenas to blue irradiation has been observed utilizing dedicated image analyze. Mobility of the microorganisms has been evaluated to decrease by nearly 30%, during blue light stimulation, with regard to the reference lightning. The experimental results have shown that OLED display, assisted by real-time image processing, may be the useful tool devoted to precise and multi-color cells irradiation.

articleTitle: Single Sensor Hot-Wire Anemometer Based on Thermal Time Constant Estimation
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: This paper presents a new type of hot-wire anemometer based on its sensor's thermal time constant estimation. In the known types of thermal anemometers, the source of measurement errors is an ambient temperature, which influences the heat exchange between the hot sensor and its surrounding fluid. Therefore, a second sensor is used to compensate the impact of ambient temperature. The solution contemplated here uses the relationship between the sensor's thermal time constant and fluid flow rate. This constant has no relationship to ambient temperature, so there is no need to use a second sensor. The paper presents algorithms for estimating the sensor's time constant, mathematical relationships, the measurement system and sample measurement results obtained.

articleTitle: Array of Gas Sensors Based on TiO2 Upon Temperature Modulation
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: The aim of this work is to demonstrate that thermal modulation improves the selectivity of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> - based resistive-type gas sensors. The sensors operate upon sinusoidal temperature profile over a temperature range of 240-300°C. Sensor array is composed of nanocrystalline TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>:Cr (0.1-10 at.% Cr). The switching from n-type to p-type conductivity occurs at about 1 at. % Cr. Electrical resistance responses to reducing and oxidizing gases such as: NO, NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub> (0-3000 ppm) are dynamically recorded and compared in order to assess cross-sensitivity as well as humidity interference. The results of the Principle Component Analysis, PCA demonstrate that reliable detection and classification of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, and NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> have been achieved.

articleTitle: Making Power over Fiber Supply of Microelectronic Sensor Devices Simpler
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Power over Fiber (PoF) supply of microelectronic sensor devices has been receiving a growing interest in recent years, especially in case of wide-area-networked microsystems, appliances working in harsh environments or exposed to thunderstorm-related disturbances as well as in sensing equipment operated under high voltage bias conditions. The paper presents a laboratory approach to construct a simple PoF supply system using off-the-shelf components, capable of delivering power required for remote supply of microprocessor-controlled low-power microelectronic sensing apparatus.

articleTitle: Inkjet 3D Printing of Labs-on-a-Chip with Optical Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Inkjet 3D printing is one of the techniques of additive manufacturing that is successfully adapted to requirements of microfluidic structures development. In this paper result of author's research works on applicability of inkjet 3D printing is described. Special attention was paid to optical properties of the printed microstructures. Than examples of various microfluidic structures are briefly described. Finally a discussion on limits and potential directions of inkjet 3D printing development for microfluidics is presented.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of LTCC Based Microfluidic Type Chemical Microreactor
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: The microfluidic type chemical microreactor was fabricated by means of low temperature co-fired ceramics. For visualization of solutions flow processes inside the microreactor channels a modeling by means of COMSOL 5.3a software was applied. It was demonstrated that for analyzed range of flow rate (1l16) local disturbance of the flow (vorticity) in the sperntine type mixer is clearly visible, reflecting in improved mixing. The computer simulations were confirmed experimentally by a rapid mixing of two fluids (dye and MilliQ water) at the chosen flow rates.

articleTitle: Copper Sulfide Materials for Nonenzymatic Glucose Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Copper sulfide materials were prepared by solvothermal technique. The structural and morphological characterization of obtained semiconductors was carried out using Scanning Electron Microscopy and X-ray diffraction method. Flower_like Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.8</sub>S was immobilized on glassy carbon electrode to construct nonenzymatic glucose sensor. Electrochemical behavior of modified electrode toward glucose was examined by cyclic voltammetry in alkaline aqueous solution. Glucose sensor exhibits a good response, high sensitivity and low detection limit for electrocatalytic oxidation of glucose.

articleTitle: TiO2/SnO2 Gas Sensors of H2
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Nanoheterostructures of n-n type based on TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> have been prepared by Flame Spray Synthesis. Basic structural and morphological properties of 50 mol. % TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/50 mol.% SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanopowders have been studied by X-ray diffraction, XRD, scanning electron microscopy SEM and transmission electron microscopy TEM. Gas sensing measurements have been carried out in a static mode under exposure to varying concentration of hydrogen within the range of 50-3000 ppm. Good sensitivity and stable responses have been detected at 350°C.

articleTitle: Spectral Dependence of the Sensitivity of Polarization Maintaining Optical Fibers to Temperature
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: The paper presents an interferometric method of measurement, which makes is possible to determine the spectral dependence of the sensitivity of the phase modal birefringence of polarization maintaining fibers (PMFs) to temperature. The method is based on the Sagnac interferometer, in whose loop only a portion of the tested PMF is subjected to temperature changes. The equation of the method of measuring the temperature sensitivity of the phase modal birefringence was derived. The sensitivity of the phase modal birefringence to temperature is determined based on a measurement of the spectral sensitivity of the interferometer to temperature. Results of measurements of the sensitivity of the birefringence to temperature as a function of wavelength are provided for two types of PM fibers: a conventional Panda-type fiber and a polarization maintaining photonic crystal fiber (PM-PCF). The results were obtained using the proposed measurement method in the temperature range 22-85°C and in the wavelength range 1280-1580 nm.

articleTitle: Accuracy Estimation of the Sounding Rocket Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Contemporary achievements in the inertial systems technology puts the question how precise consumer grade sensors are and are they sufficient to use in the navigation. The hypothetical subsonic sounding rocket will be examined, since these objects need accurate and not expensive sensors. Following types of the inertial navigation systems will be examined: based on optical gyroscope, high grade and low-grade MEMS systems. Additionally, the individual constituents of the navigation error will be examined.

articleTitle: Concept Design: Multi-Sensing System to Prevent Renal Deterioration in Heart Failure Patients
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: This paper reports a multi-sensing system that consists of two separate devices equipped with a set of multiple pressure sensors. The first device is a stent that to be inserted in the abdominal aorta; close to the renal arteries. The second one is a filter which has to be placed in the inferior vena cava, adjacent to the aortic stent. The two devices, side by side, are expected to be capable of continuously monitoring the hemodynamics, i.e., of the abdominal aorta and the inferior vena cava, in heart failure patients. This arrangement is advantageous in overcoming declination in the kidneys' functions. The multi-sensing system outputs will then be interrogated via external RF electronic hardware. Collected data from both devices allegedly will provide a comprehensive view of the current status of the heart failure patient, and alerts any possible prevalence of kidney impairment.

articleTitle: Microsystems for Cell Deformability Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: This paper presents a new technical solution in the form of MEMS-type deformation microcytometer and a new methodology for determining the deformability of animal oocytes. As a reference method compression of the oocyte with commercial micromanipulator will be descried and compared with proposed solution. Preliminary results showing the deformation of porcine oocytes will be presented using both methods to validate the work of the microcytometer.

Author Keywords: compression and indentation of the cell

articleTitle: Photonic Crystal Fiber Dynamic Pressure Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: The paper presents a polarization maintaining photonic crystal fiber sensor for dynamic pressure measurements based on a Sagnac loop filter (SLF). The SLF was illuminated by a beam reflected off a uniform fiber Bragg grating. This way a conversion of the shift of the SLF's spectrum into a change of light intensity was achieved. The pressure acting on the polarization maintaining fiber of the SLF induces a shift of its spectrum, which results in a change of the intensity of its transmitted and reflected beams in opposite directions. This makes it possible to adopt the ratio detecting method to obtain an output signal of the sensor, which is independent of light source power fluctuations. The non-linearity error of the designed and produced sensor is smaller than 1.0% in the measurement range from -0.08 to 0.2 MPa. Results of measurements of pressure steps obtained using the presented sensor are provided together with results obtained using a strain gauge sensor.

articleTitle: Technology of Stearine Transfer Using Laser-Heating for Lab-On-Paper Development
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: In this article, we demonstrate a manufacture of the lab-on-paper device. The paper presents a technology of laser thermal transfer of stearine, into a porous paper often used in chemistry. Such a rapid, one-step technology was developed to obtain a paper-based analytical device with using only paper, stearine disc and CO2 laser plotter. Melted in stearine makes hydrophobic surface which is microfluidic wall for analyzed fluids. The results show that paper-based analytical device is a cheap pH tester for a one-time use. Moreover, the whole device can be integrated with much more advanced chemicals or simple electronic for image analysis.

articleTitle: The Method for Easy Identifying Zero Temperature Drift of Catalytic Bead Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Catalytic sensors, also known as pellistors, are the most popular sensing elements measuring concentration of flammable gases in air. They are applicable in mobile and stationary instruments for indicating presence of explosive conditions in mines and other branches of industry. Among the advantages of those sensors are, for example, their linear characteristic in standard operation conditions, sensitivity to every flammable gases, lack of sensitivity toward non-flammable substances, good signal to noise ratio. However, one of their problems is fluctuation of their output signals with the change of environmental temperature. It can lead to either false alarms or lack of reactions in case of a presence of explosive conditions. To avoid such situations, the sensors are carefully selected or equipped with additional systems for compensation of the temperature drift, but identification of their thermal parameters is troublesome due to the necessity of tests performed in temperature chambers. In this paper, an alternative method of identification of the temperature dependencies is presented, based on a temperature change of the sensing element independent of ambient temperature. Physical properties of pellistors are analysed, proper dependencies are derived, and results of tests conducted on a group of the sensors are presented to show the efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: Electron Transparent Anode for MEMS Transmission Electron Microscope
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: This article describes one of the element of the miniature MEMS transmission electron microscope fully integrated on one chip, which is being developed at Faculty of Microsystem Electronics and Photonics, Wroclaw University of Science and Technology. This element is electron gun equipped with transparent anode thin silicon nitride membrane. The importance of this electrode is explained and examples of the use of such electrode are presented. The technology and parameters of thin silicon nitride membranes are presented. Finally, we describe future works, concerning the electron transparent anode, which is crucial in fabricating the miniature MEMS TEM.

articleTitle: Strain Sensor Based on a Long Period Fiber Grating with Dual-Resonance Closed in the Interferometric Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: Spectral characteristics and amplitude tunabilitity of a long period grating with a dual-resonance inside fiber loop mirror are studied in terms of applied stress caused by the elongation. Inserting the polarization controller between grating and the loop structure enables tuning of resonance and interferometric peaks. The maximum sensitivity of demonstrated sensor is 1.943 dB/mμ for the range of 1.1-4.4 mμ. Combination of these two optical components enables to measure strain in wider range in comparing with sensors based on standard long period grating.

articleTitle: MEMS Nanoleak Gas Injection System
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: In this paper different approaches to fabricate a gas injection system for miniature vacuum devices have been examined. One bases on the application of microvalves, and two others on nanoleaks through microapertures and microchannels. All of them have been prepared by the standard MEMS technology. Flow rates were investigated in large volume system and with a specially designed, integrated, miniature vacuum system.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Chip for Cyclical Continuous-Flow PCR — Preliminary Results of the Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: A new solution of glass microfluidic chip for PCR DNA amplification and pathogen detection has been proposed. A continuous-flow method has been used for rapid thermocycling of the reaction mixture at three constant temperature zones of the chip. For the first time, this process has been performed cyclically, enabling flexible change of the process parameters and application of almost unrestricted volumes of the mixture. In this paper, preliminary results on the chip operation and technology, as well as development of miniaturized setup for cyclical continuous-flow PCR process control, have been presented.

articleTitle: Influence of the Square Wave Voltage on Dynamical Properties of a Flat Voltammetric Electrode in the Time Domain by the Electrochemical Reversible Reaction
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: In this article there is a presentation of the analysis of the polarizing voltage shape influencing dynamic properties of voltammetric electrodes when on their surface reversible reaction takes place in the time domain. The electrode polarization with linearly increasing voltage and with a square component, was analyzed. The analysis that were conducted showed that the voltammetric electrode behaves like a first order transducer. Its dynamic properties in the time domain are defined by sensitivity and time constant. The results of the simulations show that these properties are determined by parameters of the voltage polarizing a voltammetric electrode.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Testing of Smart Refractory for Energy System Monitoring in Harsh-Environments
publicationTitle: 2018 XV International Scientific Conference on Optoelectronic and Electronic Sensors (COE)
abstract: To achieve better process control and efficiency for high-temperature energy systems, it is essential to monitor the conditions (temperature, pressure) and structural health (mechanical integrity) of refractory materials used in the reactors, such as within coal slagging gasifiers. Therefore, there is a need for advanced sensors capable of operating under harsh environments reliably for extended time without degrading at high temperatures. The objective of this work was to investigate embedded temperature and spallation sensors within refractory ceramic brick to operate at temperatures >1200 °C. The key aspect of the proposed technology is that the solid-state sensors used for these applications are incorporated and interconnected within the volume of the refractory and would not result in extrinsic defects through the refractory. The current paper describes the testing of the electrical performance and chemical stability of the electroceramic composite composition at the application temperatures. The paper also discusses the performance of the embedded ceramic thermistor within the “smart bricks” at temperatures up to 1400 °C, with and without the presence of molten slag.
